title: indigo_positioning_operational_moat
claim: IndiGo built dominant market share in Indian aviation by turning operational predictability into its core brand asset rather than competing on price or customer delight.
hook: This brand case study India shows how IndiGo captured 60% market share by ignoring customer delight.

reel_script.voiceover: Most airlines think passengers buy tickets on price. IndiGo proved they buy on predictability.
reel_script.direction: Rachit speaking directly to camera in a brightly lit studio.

reel_script.voiceover: In 2006, legacy carriers fought over warm meals and loyalty perks. IndiGo removed all of it.
reel_script.direction: Text overlays beside Rachit as he gestures.

reel_script.voiceover: They enforced a 25-minute ground turnaround. That kept aircraft flying 12 hours a day instead of 10.
No hot meals meant lighter aircraft, lower fuel burn, and zero kitchen equipment failures on the tarmac.
reel_script.direction: Cut to Rachit emphasizing points with hand gestures.

reel_script.voiceover: Instead of advertising comfort, every brand campaign focused on a single metric: on-time performance.
reel_script.direction: Split screen with historic IndiGo print ad graphic.

reel_script.voiceover: When reliability is your core product, competitors offering cheap tickets cannot touch your margins.
reel_script.direction: Rachit back on full screen, speaking directly to camera.

reel_script.onscreen: Send this to your brand team
reel_script.voiceover: Forward this video to a brand manager who is trying to fix positioning with discounts.
reel_script.direction: Rachit points to the share icon.

caption:
This brand case study India shows how IndiGo captured 60% market share by ignoring customer delight.

They did not win on low fares or loyalty programs. They won by cutting every amenity that delayed departure times.

By locking down a 25-minute turnaround time, IndiGo achieved 12 hours of flight time per plane daily, compared to the 10-hour industry average. Removing hot meals reduced aircraft weight and eliminated kitchen maintenance delays. They put zero positioning budget into passenger comfort and focused entirely on on-time performance metrics.

Marketing leaders often mistake delight for differentiation. Operational reliability creates a far stronger moat than subjective preference.
